column3: Contrasts induced fear with fearing Allah, sharpening the courage demanded at the gate.
An inverse gate-entry scene marks a controlled, irreversible boundary.
Frames tawakkul as remaining with Allah after delivering the message amid rejection.
Adds a gate entry joined to bodily humility and a spoken response.
Supplies the covenantal setting immediately before the entry episode.
Treats being overcome as a changeable condition, qualifying confidence about victory.
Generic belief-conditioned exhortation adds no distinct route to the focus scene.
Locates the surrounding passage in guided movement from darkness toward a straight path.
Keeps reliance on Allah alongside deliberation, giving, and measured defense.
The belief condition is not connected to entry, fear, reliance, or victory here.
Directly states the group's fear-based refusal to enter before the two men's reply.
The shared victory root occurs in an unrelated description of gardens.
Presents entry as the outcome of upright action, a secondary threshold contrast.

States a divine decree of prevailing, supporting the promise of overcoming.

Reliance after warning reiterates the mission-boundary aspect.
Moves from inward fear to increased faith and reliance on the Lord.

Contrasts fearing people with the greater claim of fearing Allah.

Begins the immediate address by recalling Allah's favors to the group.

Records the leader's separation from the refusing people immediately after 5:23-24.
Repeats conditional allegiance to victory without adding a new focus relation.

Associates allegiance to Allah with being the prevailing party.

Forbids weakness and grief while linking being uppermost to belief.
Commends those who did not weaken, yield, or submit under hardship in fighting.
Links forgiveness, firmness, and help against opponents in a communal prayer.
Transforms a warning meant to induce fear into increased faith and reliance.
Shows a return with divine favor and safety after the fear-inducing report.
Calls believers to take precautions and move out in ordered groups.
Commands action even when responsibility is limited to oneself, while urging believers onward.
Forbids losing heart in pursuit when both sides endure pain but believers hope from Allah.

Moses directs his people to seek Allah's help and be patient while facing possession of the land.

Marks retreat from the encounter as a grave boundary, except for tactical movement or joining a force.
Requires steadfastness and abundant remembrance when meeting a force, aimed at success.
Links obedience, cohesion, patience, and preservation of collective resolve.
Addresses the relation between steadfast believers and overcoming a larger opposing group.

Records how numerical confidence failed to secure victory at Hunayn.
Frames the believers' possible outcomes without conceding defeat as the only prospect.
Presents believers' struggle as a covenantal exchange with a promised outcome.
Models reliance on Allah while publicly facing an adversary's gathered plan.

Pairs patience with reliance on the Lord after pressure and displacement.

Models entrusting one's affair to Allah amid a hostile dispute.

Links support for Allah's cause to divine support and firm footing.

Connects revealed balance with iron's force and the testing of who supports Allah and His messengers.
Commends disciplined, unified ranks in struggle for Allah's cause.
Promises help from Allah and a near victory to believers.
Makes reliance the believers' response to Allah's sole divinity.
States Allah's sufficiency for whoever relies on Him.
